question.text: Under Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013, the CSR spending obligation for qualifying companies is set at what percentage of net profits?

answer.text: 1% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 3 financial years
2% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 3 financial years
2.5% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 5 financial years
5% of the average net profit of the last 1 financial year

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Section 135 of the Companies Act 2013 mandates CSR spending of 2% of the average net profit of the immediately preceding 3 financial years for qualifying companies (net worth Rs 500 cr / turnover Rs 1000 cr / net profit Rs 5 cr thresholds). **The Trap:** Options A (1%) and C (2.5%) are common confusions. Option D (5%) is fabricated. The mandate is 2%, computed on 3-year average net profit. **Cross-Exam Context:** Cross-links to X-A/X-B (Investment Adviser) for advising CSR-eligible corporates, Ch 10 (Taxation) for 80G implications on CSR-qualified donations, and V-A (MF Distributor). **Assessor's Pro-Tip:** Request the donor corporate's 'Annual CSR Report' and its CSR committee minutes to verify that CSR contributions to the SE align with Schedule VII activities. A mismatch can retroactively disqualify CSR spend — affecting impact attribution in your AIR.
